messages:
maria: heads-up — found a weird repro in the kotlin sampleapp. POST with a streaming gzip RequestBody + OkHttp 4.x + app Authenticator sometimes results in duplicate POSTs on Android emulators (only seen on API 33/34 so far). server shows two POSTs ~100ms apart with different Authorization headers. logs + minimal snippet below. anyone else seen streaming rewinds / auth races?

maria: repro details: app streams a large gziped payload (we stream to avoid OOM). flow: request sent -> server returns 401 mid-stream (token expired), our Authenticator does sync refresh -> the call retries and we see a second POST. expected: either no retry (fail) or a single retry with a replayable body. actual: duplicate POSTs and sometimes double-processing on server side.

maria: logs: 
```
[server] 2026-02-12T14:32:01.123Z POST /upload 401 - "Auth: Bearer abc_old"
[server] 2026-02-12T14:32:01.256Z POST /upload 200 - "Auth: Bearer abc_new"
```

maria: RequestBody in sampleapp: 
```kotlin
val body = object : RequestBody() {
  override fun contentType() = "application/gzip".toMediaType()
  override fun writeTo(sink: BufferedSink) {
    GzipSink(sink).use { gz -> source(inputStream).use { it.readAll(gz) } }
  }
}
```

kai: hmm. OkHttp usually won't retry a non-repeatable (streaming) body unless connection failure happens before request body write completes. If server returned 401 after request body fully sent, Authenticator might run and create a new call. But double POSTs sound like a retry path + manual retry? Do you have client config: `retryOnConnectionFailure` or an interceptor manually re-playing?

maria: client is default (retryOnConnectionFailure=true). no manual replay. Authenticator returns new request with updated header.

omar: quick thought: if the initial request fails mid-write (socket reset or server closes), okhttp may attempt a recover and replay — but replay requires buffering. streaming body isn't replayable so it shouldn't. Could it be that the server responds 401 early in the request lifecycle (before full body) so okhttp thinks safe to retry?

lina: I added a minimal test in the sampleapp that gzips from a file and hit local test server. Repro is reliable on Pixel emulator 14. Stack snippet I captured: 
```
OkHttp: call timeout set: 0
OkHttp: sending request body
Socket: write -> write returned EPIPE
Authenticator: synchronous token refresh -> new token obtained
OkHttp: recovering from connection failure -> enqueue retry
```

lina: so flow is EPIPE during body write, okhttp tries to recover and triggers a retry path while our Authenticator also returns a follow-up request — results in two attempts.

kai: that matches. two separate mechanisms: 1) connection-recovery retry (OkHttp internal) 2) Authenticator returning follow-up after 401. If both occur concurrently you can get double behavior. Usually buffering request bodies (so they are replayable) avoids partial-state issues, or turn off retryOnConnectionFailure.

maria: turning off retryOnConnectionFailure worked in my local run (single failure). but we can't require buffering large payloads in mobile — defeats streaming memory benefit.

omar: another angle: ensure token refresh is single-flight so multiple concurrent callers don't trigger separate refreshes. If Authenticator blocks other calls until refresh finishes, you may avoid duplicate auth flows. Also consider doing token refresh outside of Authenticator (interceptor + suspend mutex) so streaming write isn't interrupted.

lina: quick code snippet we used as a workaround (mutex around refresh). not perfect but reduces repro: 
```kotlin
private val refreshMutex = Mutex()
suspend fun refreshTokenSafe() {
  refreshMutex.withLock {
    if (tokenExpired()) { doRefresh() }
  }
}
// AuthenticatorBridge calls refreshTokenSafe() via runBlocking
```

kai: FYI: Authenticator interface is synchronous so we often end up calling suspend -> runBlocking which can block okio threads. Prefer pre-refresh in an Interceptor that can suspend (when using okhttp coroutines adapter) or use a synchronized cache. Also consider using `NetworkInterceptor` to detect 401s earlier.

maria: thanks — good notes. two actionable paths: 1) add a sampleapp showcase that uses a streaming safe pattern (chunk + resume test) and docs warning about `retryOnConnectionFailure` + streaming bodies, or 2) change sample Authenticator to single-flight refresh + avoid runBlocking on IO threads.

omar: also add integration test on emulator farm for API 33/34 to catch EPIPE + retry combos (CI flaky currently).

ci-bot: CI notice: reproducible-test-upload branch failed on emulator-14 matrix: `UploadRetryRaceTest` (see PR #1212).

maria: I'll open a small PR that (a) disables retryOnConnectionFailure in the sampleapp client config, (b) adds a note in devex docs about streaming + auth races, and (c) provides the mutex-based Authenticator example. cc @kai @lina for review. :thumbsup:

kai: sounds good. also add a short snippet showing how to buffer a small initial prefix (e.g., first 8KB) so retries can fast-fail without re-sending huge payloads. saves memory but gives retry safety.

lina: added to backlog. thanks all :sparkles:
